findings.label: Alopecia (hair loss)
findings.evidence: Alopecia in biotinidase deficiency; 'the child had normal neurological findings, except for hypotonia, irritability and alopecia [Figure 1]'

panels.rationale: Single clinical photograph of an infant showing near-total scalp hair loss (alopecia), the captioned manifestation of biotinidase deficiency in this case report; the article title and caption attribute the alopecia directly to biotinidase deficiency. Face is shown with eyes redacted for privacy; skin appears light-toned and adequately lit.
panels.attribution_text: Bhardwaj et al. Biotinidase deficiency: A treatable cause of infantile seizures.. Journal of pediatric neurosciences 2010. doi:10.4103/1817-1745.66660. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
in_text_mentions: e child developed normally for the first 3 months and after that was not growing normally. On examination, the child had normal neurological findings, except for hypotonia, irritability and alopecia [Figure 1]. The child also had a mild developmental delay. Laboratory investigations revealed normal hemogram, liver functions, serum ammonia and serum electrolytes. Blood gas analysis showed metabolic acidosis and the baby also had persistent ketonuria, while cerebrospinal fluid examination was normal.
